a.method.net-pnl: Sum of net profit and loss across all trades closed in the period. Net means after commission and swap, so it is what actually reached the account balance.
a.method.return-percent: Net P&L for the period divided by account equity at the start of the period. Deposits and withdrawals made during the period are excluded from the denominator.
a.method.trade-count: Number of positions fully closed within the period.
a.method.win-rate: Winning trades divided by trades that finished with a non-zero result. Break-even trades are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator.
a.method.profit-factor: Total profit from winning trades divided by total loss from losing trades. Above 1.0 means the winners outweighed the losers over this period.
a.method.expectancy: Average net result per closed trade over the period. It describes what happened, not what will happen.
a.method.average-winner: Mean net profit across winning trades only.
a.method.average-loser: Mean net loss across losing trades only. Shown as a negative amount.
a.method.average-risk-reward: Average winning trade divided by the size of the average losing trade. A value of 2.0 means a typical win was twice the size of a typical loss.
a.method.max-drawdown: Largest fall from a peak in account equity to the following low, measured on the closed-trade equity curve. Floating losses on positions that were still open are not included, so a live account may have dipped further intraday.
a.method.recovery-factor: Net P&L for the period divided by the maximum drawdown. It indicates how much return was produced for each unit of peak-to-trough decline endured.
a.method.position-size-consistency: How similar the money you planned to risk was from trade to trade. For each trade with a stop-loss, we take the loss that stop would have produced and divide it by your account equity just before the trade opened. The score is 1 minus the variation in those figures, scaled to 100: a score of 100 means every trade risked the same share of your account. Lot size is deliberately not used, because the same number of lots means a completely different amount of money in gold, EURUSD and an index. Trades without a stop-loss have no planned risk and are excluded — they are counted under "Trades with a stop-loss".
a.method.average-risk-per-trade: For each trade that had a stop-loss, the amount that would have been lost at the stop, expressed as a percentage of account equity immediately before the trade opened, then averaged. Trades without a stop-loss are excluded because their risk was not defined.
a.method.stop-loss-usage-rate: Share of closed trades that had a stop-loss attached at any point before closing.
a.method.stop-loss-outcome-delta: Average net result of trades that had a stop-loss, minus the average net result of trades that did not. This is an association within your own trade history over this period, not proof that one caused the other.
a.method.post-loss-size-change: Average percentage change in position size between a losing trade and the next trade opened after it closed. Overlapping positions are excluded because neither followed the other. A positive value means size tended to increase.
a.method.post-win-size-change: Average percentage change in position size between a winning trade and the next trade opened after it closed. Overlapping positions are excluded because neither followed the other. A positive value means size tended to increase.
a.method.rapid-reentry-rate: Share of losing trades that were followed by a new position in the same instrument within five minutes of the loss being closed. It describes timing only, and says nothing about why the trade was taken.
a.method.overtrading-days: Number of days on which you opened more trades than twice your own median for an active day. The threshold is relative to your usual activity, not a fixed number.
a.method.total-spread-cost: The part of each trade result attributable to the bid/ask spread, calculated as the difference between the trade result and what the same trade would have returned at the mid price.
a.method.total-commission: Sum of commission charged on every trade closed in the period, as recorded on each trade. Shown as a negative amount because it was deducted from your result.
a.method.total-swap: Sum of overnight financing across all trades closed in the period. Positive values mean financing was credited to you rather than charged.
a.method.total-trading-cost: Commission plus swap across every trade closed in the period. This is what trading cost you before any market movement is taken into account.
a.method.concentration-top-symbol: Share of total traded volume in the single most-traded instrument over the period. The instrument was {symbol}.
a.method.correlated-exposure: Share of traded volume falling within a single group of instruments that typically move together. Groups are a fixed, published mapping rather than a computed correlation, so this is indicative. The largest group was {group}.

prop.payoutStatusWaitingBody: This request has been received and is waiting for the programme to confirm or reject it. Nothing is sent twice while we wait.

prop.appealFailed: We could not record your request. Nothing has been sent — please try again.

robots.title: Automated trading
robots.homeTitle: Let a robot follow your rules
robots.homeBody: Set the conditions and the limits, watch it on demo, then run it on one account you choose.
robots.homeBodyActive: See what it has done and how close it is to the ceilings you set.
robots.buildBody: Turn clear rules into a strategy you can inspect and test.
robots.noneBody: A robot follows rules you set, on one account you choose.
robots.routeDescribeBody: Coach asks for missing rules and creates an editable draft.
robots.routeBuildBody: Set entry, exit and risk conditions yourself.
robots.describePrompt: Describe the strategy in your own words.
robots.describePlaceholder: Buy gold when the EMA crosses, stop loss 20, target 40
robots.describeNotAi: Your words are matched against rules this app can actually run. Nothing is sent to an AI service.
robots.rulesInstrumentCount: {count} of {total} instruments can be tested in this demo. A robot can be built on any of them.
robots.rulesInstrumentUnsupportedWhy: No price history or trading costs in this demo yet
robots.rulesInstrumentMore: Showing {shown} of {total} matches. Refine the search to see more.
robots.rulesInstrumentUntestedTitle: You can build this robot, not test it yet
robots.rulesInstrumentUntestedBody: This demo has no price history or trading costs for {symbol}, so the robot cannot be backtested or run here. Everything else can be set up now.
robots.rulesEntryNone: No entry signal is set. Choose one: a robot with nothing to open a trade on never places one.
robots.rulesProblemsBody: The engine will not guess at a rule it cannot read, and nothing is estimated while one is unresolved.
robots.rulesUnavailable: This draft cannot be edited here.
robots.backtestBody: A deterministic replay over the demo price series. It is a fixture, not a forecast, and past behaviour does not predict future results.
robots.backtestDataBody: A synthetic price series generated for this build and fixed by version. It is not market history, and no result here is a forecast.
robots.backtestCosts: Spread and commission are charged on every trade.
robots.backtestCostModelBody: Spread {spread}, half charged on each side of every fill, and commission of {commission} per lot per side: the costs the order ticket quotes for {symbol}.
robots.backtestConvertedAt: Converted into {account} at the fixed test rate of 1 {account} = {rate} {profit}.
robots.backtestRefusedByLimitsBody: Entries these rules asked for that your own limits would not have allowed. Change a limit and run the test again to see the difference.
robots.blockStaleData: The price data was too old to act on
robots.blockDailyLoss: The daily loss limit had been reached
robots.blockMaxOrders: The daily order limit had been reached
robots.blockMaxPositions: The open position limit had been reached
robots.backtestOpenAtEnd: One position was still open at the last bar. It is not counted in any figure above.
robots.backtestNoTrades: These rules placed no trades on this data

robots.backtestRefused: This strategy cannot be replayed yet
robots.backtestRefusedBody: Nothing is estimated in the meantime. Correct the rules below and run the test again.

robots.demoFlatAtEnd: No position was open at the last bar
robots.demoPracticeOnly: Practice only. This test places nothing on any account, live or demo, and creates no order anywhere.

robots.demoRefused: This strategy cannot be tested yet
robots.demoRefusedBody: Correct the rules first. Nothing is simulated in the meantime.

robots.accountOnlyOrx: Robots are available on ORX brokerage accounts only.
robots.accountOpenBody: Keep robot activity separate from manual trades.
robots.accountNoneBody: A robot runs on an ORX brokerage account. Open one to continue; MT4, MT5 and challenge accounts cannot be robot destinations.
robots.openAccountBody: This uses the standard account-opening journey. The new account starts at zero and is funded the normal way.
robots.openAccountReadyBody: The account exists and holds nothing. Fund it before enabling a robot on it.
robots.openAccountNoneBody: Nothing was opened, so there is nothing to fund or point a robot at. Start the account again, or choose one you already have.
robots.openAccountUse: Use this account for the robot
robots.openAccountUsed: This robot will run on this account
robots.openAccountIneligible: This account cannot run a robot
robots.openAccountIneligibleBody: The robot has not been pointed at it, and nothing has been moved. Choose an eligible account instead.
robots.openAccountUnfunded: It holds nothing yet. A robot on an empty account will be refused for margin on its first order — funding it is a separate step and no money has been moved for you.

robots.runnerActive: Running while this screen is open
robots.runnerActiveBody: This preview advances the robot only while you are on a robot screen. Nothing runs in the background, and leaving does not change what has already been placed.

robots.reviewExecutionValue: While a robot screen is open · Deterministic rules

robots.reviewConsent: I understand automated trading places real orders under these rules, and can lose more than the control estimates suggest.

robots.refusal.platformNotOrx: Robots run on ORX accounts. This account is on MetaTrader.
robots.refusal.accountIsProp: A challenge account cannot run a robot.
robots.refusal.accountIsDemo: Robots run on live ORX accounts, and this one is a demo account.
robots.refusal.accountNotActive: This account is not active, so a robot cannot trade on it.
robots.refusal.accountUnknown: That account is no longer on your profile.
robots.refusal.rulesUnsupported: These rules cannot be run yet. Go back to the rules step and complete or correct the highlighted rule.
robots.refusal.termsOutdated: The robot terms were updated after you agreed. Read the summary again and agree to the current terms.
robots.refusal.limitsInvalid: These limits cannot be run. Go back to the limits step and set a positive lot size, position count, order count and daily loss cap.
robots.refusal.consentInvalid: Your agreement could not be matched to this account. Read the summary again and agree once more.
robots.pauseFailedBody: Nothing has changed: the robot is exactly as it was before you pressed. Check your connection and press the button again.
robots.describeFailedBody: Nothing was saved. Your description is still here, so check your connection and press Continue again.
robots.stopFailedBody: Nothing has changed: the robot is still running exactly as before. Check your connection and press Stop robot again.

robots.enableFailed: We could not switch this robot on

robots.reviewCompletedBody: {name} was enabled from this setup and is now managed from its own page. Nothing here is waiting for you.
robots.reviewStale: The rules or the account changed after you agreed. Read the summary again before enabling.
robots.reviewNotReady: Choose the account this robot will trade on before you agree. Consent is recorded against a specific account, so it cannot be given without one.
robots.noOwnedPositionsBody: Nothing on this account is open under this robot right now. The account may hold other positions — placed by you, by a copied strategy or by another robot — and those are not this robot’s.
robots.showAllPositions: Show all positions on this account
robots.filteredToRobotBody: These are the positions opened by {robot}. Other positions on this account are hidden.

marketPlay.story.noPremature: No result notification is sent until the scoring window and required sources are complete.
marketPlay.story.earlyReadNotice: This is provisional. It can change when the full window closes.
marketPlay.story.revisedNotice: Later evidence weakened the earlier explanation. We revised the story rather than keeping a confident but incomplete claim.
marketPlay.story.insufficientBody: The signals do not point to one defensible explanation. We will not invent one.
marketPlay.story.insufficientScorable: Your prediction can still be scored. Direction and the reaction window are objective. The causal explanation remains unconfirmed and will update only if the evidence improves.
marketPlay.story.notifyIfClear: Notify me if the story becomes clear
marketPlay.story.correlationNotice: Likely drivers, not proven causes. The story updates as corroborating evidence changes.
marketPlay.story.advanceRefusedRelease: The scheduled release has not happened yet.
marketPlay.story.advanceRefusedPredictio: Predictions are still being taken on this story.
marketPlay.story.advanceRefusedWindow: The measurement window this step reports on has not closed.
marketPlay.story.advanceRefusedEvidence: A source this explanation would rest on has not arrived.
marketPlay.story.advanceRefusedComplete: Every required source arrived, so there is nothing left unexplained.
marketPlay.story.advanceRefusedRevision: There is nothing new to revise this explanation with.
marketPlay.story.advanceRefusedTerminal: This story has reached the end of its published lifecycle.
marketPlay.story.advanceRefusedOrder: The lifecycle does not permit that step.
marketPlay.outcome.title: Outcome
marketPlay.outcome.measuredCaption: Objective and independent of any explanation.
marketPlay.outcome.edgePointsCaption: Educational only. Edge points are not cash, cannot be traded, withdrawn or converted, and never depend on deposits, volume, size, leverage or profit and loss.
marketPlay.outcome.rubricFixed: The evidence rubric was registered before the result was known.
marketPlay.outcome.pendingBody: This play has not produced a verified result.
marketPlay.crowd.title: How others read it
marketPlay.crowd.hiddenUntilLocked: Community choices were hidden until your prediction locked, protecting independent judgment.
marketPlay.crowd.noLeaderboard: No follower counts, profit-and-loss leaderboard, public shaming or reward for being contrarian. The comparison teaches calibration.
marketPlay.crowd.lockedUntilAnsweredBody: The community distribution stays hidden until you lock your own prediction. Seeing it first would not be your judgment.
marketPlay.crowd.lockedUntilResolvedBody: Your answer is locked. The comparison opens when the play resolves.

marketPlay.replay.paused: The chart is paused. Make the cleanest decision from what was visible at that moment.
marketPlay.replay.question: What would you do here?
marketPlay.replay.hiddenNotice: The continuation is not sent to your device until your choice is locked.
marketPlay.replay.practiceOnly: A practice decision. No order is created.

marketPlay.states.offlineBody: It was stored before the cutoff. Reconnect to receive the verified result and explanation.
marketPlay.states.offlineNotLockedBody: You are offline and no prediction was sent, so nothing has been recorded for this play.
